lines.text: What happens to an entire metropolitan city when a critical suspension bridge suddenly shuts down at 5 PM?
Modern highway networks function like complex hydraulic systems under extreme pressure.
When a bridge carrying one hundred thousand cars daily closes, traffic doesn't just stop; it detonates backwards.
GPS navigation algorithms frantically reroute tens of thousands of vehicles onto narrow suburban side streets.
Neighborhood roads gridlock instantly, trapping emergency ambulances, fire trucks, and city buses.
A single point of failure can paralyze an entire metro economy for twenty straight miles.
It proves just how dependent our cities are on a handful of steel and concrete arteries.
